Methods

Data

This study uses Patient-Generated Health Data (PGHD) from the VA Wearable Technology Program, in which Veterans voluntarily enrolled and shared wearable device data (Fitbit, Garmin, or Apple Health). Data were obtained from January 01, 2022 through May 14, 2026. Daily step counts from Fitbit and Garmin devices were prioritized (using the higher value when both were present); Apple Health data served as an alternative when Fitbit/Garmin data were unavailable. A total of NA patient-days had usable step data; Fitbit/Garmin data were available for NA% and Apple Health for the remainder. Daily step counts of zero were treated as missing, and outliers were removed using the 1.5””IQR method applied to raw device columns. Where step data were missing but exercise duration (minutes) was recorded, steps were imputed from a linear regression model fit on matched days (steps ~ exercise_minutes).

Cohort Derivation (Figure 1)

The analytic cohort was drawn from Veterans with PGHD records available from January 01, 2022 through May 14, 2026 (Step 0: N = 8,038). We then restricted to patients with first PGHD upload between January 01, 2022 and February 13, 2026 (Step 1), where the upper bound is set to preserve full 30-day outcome ascertainment before the data extract end date. Weekly rows were required to have at least one day of step data (Step 2: k_steps_7d_miss_days <= 6). No minimum baseline-duration requirement was applied in Study 2; all Step-2 qualifying person-weeks were retained before censoring (Step 3). Observation windows were censored at the first composite event or at 12 weeks after first upload, whichever came first (Step 4). The final analytic cohort included 4,700 Veterans contributing NA person-weeks of observation.

Step Feature Construction

At each observation week, a suite of step-derived features was computed from the 7-day, 14-day, and 21-day rolling windows anchored to the calendar week end-date. The primary current-activity features include the 7-day rolling average daily step count (k_steps_7d_avg, thousands), the rolling standard deviation (k_steps_7d_sd), the number of missing days in the window (k_steps_7d_miss_days), and the count of days with fewer than 1,000 steps (low_activity_days_7d). A temporal change metric captures short-term trend: percent change from the average of the prior three 7-day windows (k_steps_7d_avg_pctdiff, winsorized at plus or minus 500%). Analogous 14-day and 21-day rolling averages and standard deviations provide longer-horizon smoothed signals.

Outcome Definition

The primary outcome was a composite of ED visit, inpatient admission, or death occurring within the prediction horizon (\(h\) = 14 or 30 days) following a given observation week’s end date. The outcome was labeled positive (\(Y = 1\)) if any component occurred within 1 to \(h\) days (days_to_event \(\in [1, h]\)), and negative (\(Y = 0\)) otherwise. For each prediction horizon \(h\), observation weeks for non-event patients were excluded if fewer than \(h\) days remained before the end of the patient’s observation window, as the outcome classification could not be confirmed over the full horizon. This ensures that 14-day models retain more person-weeks than 30-day models for the same patients.

Statistical Analysis

We fit three feature sets: (1) step-derived features only; (2) static clinical features only (demographics, comorbidity flags, prior healthcare utilization, vitals, labs, and social history); and (3) the combined set. For each feature set and each prediction horizon (14-day and 30-day), we trained two algorithm types: penalized logistic regression (with elastic-net preprocessing) and gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost). Patients were randomly assigned to training (70%) and testing (30%) sets; all observation-weeks for a given patient remained in the same partition. To address class imbalance, logistic regression models were trained on patient-level 3:1 undersampled data; XGBoost models were trained on the full (non-undersampled) training data with scale_pos_weight set to the true negative-to-positive ratio, avoiding the probability compression that results from training and scoring on different class distributions.

To ensure accurate absolute risk estimates, predicted probabilities were calibrated using Platt scaling (logistic regression of observed outcomes on raw model log-odds). Calibration models were fit on a held-out 20% of training patients (patient-level split, preserving the original class distribution) and applied to the independent test set, ensuring no test-set information was used to fit the calibration model. All discrimination and calibration metrics were computed on the Platt-calibrated test-set probabilities. Model performance was evaluated using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC), the Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (PR-AUC), the post-calibration slope (target: 1.0), and the Brier Skill Score (BSS = 1 \(-\) Brier/Brier\(_{\text{null}}\), where Brier\(_{\text{null}}\) = \(\bar{p}(1-\bar{p})\)). BSS accounts for the low baseline event rate (<3% per week): BSS = 0 indicates no improvement over a null model predicting the marginal event rate, and BSS = 1 indicates perfect probabilistic skill. The pre-calibration slope is additionally reported as a diagnostic of raw model output compression.

To evaluate whether the primary model captures predictive signal from weeks with sparse device engagement, test-set predictions were stratified post-hoc by weekly data quality: “clean” weeks (0–3 missing days; greater than 4 days with step data) and “sparse” weeks (4–6 missing days; 1–3 days with step data). Discrimination and skill metrics (AUC, PR-AUC, BSS) were computed separately for each stratum without model refit, directly testing whether weeks with low device engagement (which may reflect pre-event health deterioration) are predicted as effectively as high-quality weeks.

Figure 4. ROC Curves and AUC Summary: 14-Day and 30-Day Horizons

Figure 4. ROC curves at 30-day horizon for logistic regression and XGBoost across feature sets.

Figure 5. XGBoost Feature Importance: Steps + Static Model

Figure 5. Top 20 XGBoost feature importances (Gain): Steps + Static, 14-Day and 30-Day Horizons. Bars filled by feature category (colorblind-friendly Set2 palette). Gain = fractional contribution to total information gain across all trees. Labels show Gain x 100.

Figure 6. Logistic Regression Coefficients: Steps + Static Model

Figure 6. Top 20 elastic net-regularized logistic regression coefficients (OR scale, per 1 SD for continuous predictors): Steps + Static, 14-Day and 30-Day Horizons. Colored by feature category (Set2 palette). These are penalized estimates and should be interpreted as directional associations reflecting relative feature importance within the model, not formal hypothesis tests.

Note: Coefficients are elastic net-penalized estimates (glmnet, Steps + Static model). Penalization shrinks estimates toward zero and the plot carries no inferential standard errors or significance thresholds; values reflect the direction and relative magnitude of each feature’s contribution within the regularized model. A full coefficient table is saved to logistic_coefficients_14d_30d.xlsx.
